slides.label: WHY THE FIRST LINE MATTERS
lines: "Thank you for choosing us" gets skimmed. "I keep coming back to that bull on day four" gets read.
Email 1 has one job: be remembered. The opening line does most of it.

slides.label: EMAIL 1 · WHERE THE MOMENT GOES
slides.sub: Send within a week of the hunt ending. No ask in this one.
slides.subject: Thank you from [Camp name]
body: Thanks for hunting with us. I keep coming back to [ONE REAL MOMENT].
I'm sorting through photos and will send you the good ones this week. Safe travels home.
slides.note: That bracket is the whole trick. Here are six things to put in it.

slides.label: OPENERS 1 AND 2
items: "…that bull at first light on day four."
"…the long pack out. You never complained once."

slides.label: OPENERS 3 AND 4
items: "…that morning the snow came in sideways and we kept going."

slides.label: OPENERS 5 AND 6
items: "…watching you and your dad glass that basin together."
"…those ten minutes on the ridge when nobody said a word."

slides.label: FILLED IN · MOCK NAMES
slides.sub: Same email, one real moment, nothing to sell.
slides.subject: Thank you from [Camp name]
body: Thanks for hunting with us. I keep coming back to that evening on the ridge when three bulls were screaming at each other and you didn't say a word for ten minutes.
I'm sorting photos and I'll send the good ones this week. Safe travels. — Tom

slides.label: FOUR WAYS TO MISS
items: The thank-you has to be a thank-you.
Ask your guide. A wrong detail is worse than none.
Send it within a week, while they still feel it.
